data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is primarily a boundary-layer depth effect. On clear, calm nights, the rural boundary layer becomes extremely shallow and stable, trapping the small amount of cooling in a thin layer near the ground. The urban boundary layer, kept well-mixed by the urban canopy's roughness and by ongoing anthropogenic and stored-heat release, remains deeper. The temperature difference is therefore an artifact of comparing a shallow, rapidly cooling rural layer with a deeper, well-mixed urban one. The single best cross-city predictor is city size: larger cities generate a deeper, more persistent urban boundary layer and a stronger heat-island circulation, making the nocturnal gap more pronounced.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If urban and rural boundary-layer depths are similar (e.g., in very light wind with uniform roughness), the depth-differential mechanism collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If measurement heights are well above both boundary layers (e.g., on tall towers or rooftops), the near-surface amplification disappears.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If rural roughness is high (e.g., forested countryside), the rural boundary layer may also remain well-mixed, eliminating the contrast.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under clear, calm conditions, the rural surface cools radiatively, forming a very shallow, stable nocturnal boundary layer in which temperature drops sharply with height. The urban surface, warmed by stored sensible heat release and anthropogenic emissions, maintains turbulent mixing and a deeper, less stable boundary layer. The measured near-surface temperature gap is amplified because the rural sensor sits in a thin, cold layer while the urban sensor sits in a deeper, well-mixed layer. This effect scales with city size: larger cities sustain a deeper urban boundary layer and a stronger UHI circulation, producing a larger nocturnal temperature differential.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
